# Council Bill CB 26-0177 (Introduced)

## Sponsorship

Council Member [Redacted], First District.

## Title

An Ordinance concerning **Annual Lead-Paint Inspections — Rental Units
Constructed Before 1978** for the purpose of amending Title 14 of the
Baltimore City Code to require certified annual lead-paint inspections of
covered rental units, prescribing inspection certificates and tenant
notification, providing for civil penalties for non-compliance, and
generally relating to public-health protections for residents of
pre-1978 rental housing.

## Section 1 — Title 14, Subtitle 3, Section 14-301 (new)

Every rental unit located within Baltimore City and constructed before
January 1, 1978, shall receive a certified lead-paint inspection within
twelve (12) months of the effective date of this ordinance, and annually
thereafter. The owner of such a unit shall arrange the inspection through
a contractor certified by the Maryland Department of the Environment.

The owner shall provide the tenant with a copy of the inspection
certificate within thirty (30) days of the inspection date. The
certificate shall include the inspection date, the name and certification
number of the inspecting contractor, the inspected areas of the unit, and
any remediation actions recommended.

## Section 2 — Title 14, Subtitle 3, Section 14-302 (new)

Failure to provide an inspection certificate as required under Section
14-301 subjects the owner to a civil penalty of five hundred dollars
($500.00) per unit per month of non-compliance, payable to the Baltimore
City General Fund. The Department of Housing and Community Development
shall enforce this section. Penalty proceeds collected under this
section shall be deposited in a dedicated subaccount of the General Fund
designated for lead-paint abatement programs.

## Section 3 — Title 14, Subtitle 3, Section 14-303 (new)

The Commissioner of Health may, by regulation, exempt classes of rental
units from the inspection requirement upon a finding that the units pose
no measurable lead-paint hazard. Any such regulation shall be published
in the City Register at least 30 days before taking effect and shall be
subject to Council review.

## Section 4 — Effective Date

This ordinance shall take effect ninety (90) days after the date of its
final passage and approval by the Mayor.

## Sponsor's Statement

Lead-paint exposure remains a documented public-health threat to
children in pre-1978 rental housing in Baltimore City. Existing inspection
requirements are triggered only by tenant complaint, leaving units
without complaining tenants un-inspected for decades. This ordinance
closes the enforcement gap by requiring proactive annual inspection of
all covered units, providing tenants with documentation of their unit's
status, and creating a funded enforcement mechanism via civil-penalty
proceeds.
